messages.subject: Re: 1) breaking the legend in two columns and 2) labeller option
parts:
Hi:

Given the lengths of the labels of the contiguity variable, I'd
suggest a one-column legend. Here's my stab at your request.

library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)

cols <- rainbow(13, s = 1, v = 1, start = 0, end = max(1, 13 - 1)/13, alpha = 1)
label_s <- c("20km","50km","100km","5 Nearest Neigh.","10 Nearest Neigh.",
"15 Nearest Neigh.","Sphere of Influence","Gabriel Graph",
"Relative Graph","First Order Queen W","Second Order Queen W",
"First Order Rook W","Second Order Rook W")

# Define the following as factor variables; the second labels the
# levels to correspond to the age ranges you requested
DF$OrderPlot <- factor(DF$order_plot, levels = seq(13))
DF$AgeGp <- factor(DF$data.var, labels = c("15-19", "20-24", "25-29"))

# This stacks the two Moran measures so that you can use the resulting
# 'variable' as a factor to map to linetypes, eliminating the extra
geom_line() call.
DFm <- melt(DF, measure = c("MoranI", "MoranI.sig"))

ggplot(DFm, aes(x=Year))+
geom_line(aes(y=value, colour=OrderPlot, size=OrderPlot,
linetype= variable))+
scale_size_manual(name="Contiguity",
values = c(rep(0.5, 11) ,1.2, 0.5),
labels=label_s) +
labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(1981, 1985, 1990, 1995, 2000, 2005, 2011),
limits=c(1981,1986))+
scale_colour_manual(name = 'Contiguity', values = cols, labels=label_s) +
scale_linetype_manual(values = c("solid", "dotted")) +
guides(linetype = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 1)))+
facet_wrap(~ AgeGp, ncol=3)

In this case, a one-column legend for contiguity minimizes the space
required for the legend and thus maximizes the area for the graph. If
you try to stack the legend labels into several columns, most of the
graphics space will be taken up by the legends. I think this plot is
OK, but YMMV. I did try to use multiple rows/cols with guide_legend(),
but ggplot2 silently ignored it.

I put NULL in as the value for the x/y labels to remove the space used
for them; if you want it back, just replace NULL with "". The
override.aes argument was used to increase the size of the linetypes
in the legend.

Not included here, but I'd suggest adding theme_bw() after the first
line. The default background makes it hard to see the green lines -
they're easier to spot with theme_bw().

Dennis

messages.subject: breaking the legend in two columns? guide_legend seems not to work...
parts:
Thanks for your answer!
My want for multiple columns is that my ‘real’ number of panels (the dput-ed dataset is a subset otherwise it would be way longer) is 7 over 3 columns (3*3) so that would have two empty panels for it, and it would look much better in this case. And yes, theme_bw makes it look much better!
guide_legend (what online tutorials suggest) seems to just be ignored by ggplot, I wonder if this feature is not available anymore or else?

messages.author: 99e3ad08a7577760
messages.subject: Re: breaking the legend in two columns? guide_legend seems not to work...
parts:
I’ve spent some time trying to figure out why it worked and now it seems I got it the right way. Basically, I have added it to scale_size_manual and scale_colour_manual. Why it works now, this was it’s kind of foggy but it works well, so I’ll keep it.

Ale

so for future reference, here is the code:

ggplot(DF, aes(x=Year))+
  geom_line(aes(y=value,colour=factor(order_plot),size=factor(order_plot)),linetype=1)+
  scale_size_manual(name="Contiguity Type",values = c(0.5,0.5,0.5,0.5,0.5,0.5,0.5,0.5,0.5,0.5,0.5,1.2,0.5,0.5),labels=label_select,guide=guide_legend(nrow=7))+
  geom_line(aes(y=MoranI.sig,colour=factor(order_plot),size=factor(order_plot)),linetype=1)+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(1981,1990,2000,2011),limits=c(1981,2011))+
  scale_colour_manual(name = 'Contiguity Type', values = col,labels=label_select,guide=guide_legend(nrow=7))+
  scale_fill_discrete(name="legendName")+
  facet_wrap(~data.var,ncol=3)
